title: Agent Test Specification
description: The OpenSpec artifact emitted from one scenario record. It states what the testing agent does, where it is allowed to do it, what the lab must replicate, and what artifacts each step should produce. GENERATED by tools/emit_testspec.py; never hand edited. Regenerate it instead. The spec is the instruction set; the sealed prediction alongside it is the claim being tested, and the two are deliberately separate files so the prediction can be committed before the run and never silently revised afterwards.

spec_version.description: Bump only on breaking change to this artifact's shape.

spec_id.description: Spec id, ST plus the scenario number. One current spec per scenario per baseline.

scenario.description: The scenario record this was emitted from.

baseline.description: The framework baseline the scenario spoke when this was emitted. A spec is not comparable across baselines.

source_digest.description: sha256 of the scenario record file as emitted from. If the scenario changes, this spec is stale and must be regenerated: a run against a stale spec scores a prediction nobody makes any more.

status.description: draft: emitted, not authorized. approved: an accountable human authorized the run. executed: a run record references it. superseded: the scenario moved on.

authorization.description: The guardrail block. This is what makes the same spec safe to run in a lab today and reviewable for production later. Nothing here is decoration: the emitter refuses to mark a spec approved without it, and an executor that cannot honor every field must refuse the run.

autonomy.description: The same ladder the use case record uses, for the same reason: it is earned with measured evidence, one rung at a time, never declared. lab-only: designated ephemeral lab targets only. production-observe: benign signal generation against production to test the real detection pipeline, no state change, no adversary action. production-active: bounded actions against production; requires the promotion block.

enabled_rungs.description: Which rungs this deployment has actually turned on. In the prototype this is ['lab-only'] and the executor must refuse anything above it, even if a spec asks.

targets.description: The explicit allowlist. An empty list means nothing may run: there is no default target and no wildcard. Anything not named here is out of scope, and reaching it is a stop condition.

id.description: The lab identifier: namespace, cluster, account or host label.

scope_note.description: What this target stands in for, and what it deliberately does not.

time_box.description: ISO 8601 duration. The agent stops when it expires, whether or not the procedure finished. An unfinished run is a data point; an unbounded run is an incident.

egress.description: Lab network policy. deny-all is the default and the right answer for almost every scenario. allowlist requires the destinations to be named in targets and justified in fidelity_notes.

stop_conditions.description: Conditions that abort the run immediately and leave the environment for inspection. At minimum: any interaction with an address outside the allowlist, any credential that resolves outside the lab, any action not in the procedure, and time box expiry.

teardown_required.description: Whether the environment must be destroyed and the destruction asserted in the run record. True for every lab-ephemeral target.

prohibited.description: Stated for the reader and for the executor's own checks. The standing set: no exploit development, no unpublished vulnerability research, no action against a system not in targets, no persistence that survives teardown, no exfiltration of real data (synthetic canaries only).

promotion.description: REQUIRED when autonomy is above lab-only. Deliberately the same shape as the use case promotion block, because it answers the same question on the same day: how did anyone decide this was safe to run unattended.

clean_runs.description: Runs completed at the lower rung with no stop condition triggered and clean teardown.

environment_faults.description: Times the run damaged or failed to release the environment. A non-zero count does not block promotion by itself, but it must be read aloud.

disable.description: How this is turned off and who can do it, in one sentence a person can act on under pressure.

environment.description: What a lab has to reproduce for this run to mean anything. Derived from the scenario's steps and evidence rows, so it is a requirement list rather than a wish list.

layer.description: L0 Infrastructure, L1 Data, L2 Model, L3 Orchestration and Agent, or L4 Application.

components.description: The concrete things that must exist for a step to be executable at all.

fidelity.description: exact: the same product and version as production, because the artifact depends on it. equivalent: any implementation of the same class. stub: a stand-in that only has to accept the interaction. Getting this wrong in the cheap direction is the most common way a lab result stops transferring.

telemetry_pipeline.description: The most important block in the spec, and the one most likely to be skipped. A lab that reproduces the target but not the logging path can only test whether an artifact CAN exist, never whether WE would see it. Which claims a run is allowed to score follows directly from this field.

mode.description: mirrored: the lab ships to the same collectors, parsers and detection content as production, so detection claims are testable. scratch: the lab collects locally with its own tooling, so only signal presence and source attribution are testable. none: no collection, so nothing about our estate is testable and the run can only confirm that a technique executes.

required_sources.description: The exact systems named on the scenario's evidence rows. In mirrored mode every one of these must exist in the lab or the corresponding claim is unscoreable and must be recorded as such rather than assumed.

fidelity_notes.description: Known gaps between this lab and the estate the scenario was scored against. Every entry here is a caveat on the scorecard, so writing them down is what keeps the calibration number honest.

procedure.description: What the agent does, one entry per testable scenario step, in order. Deliberately engine agnostic: it states intent, technique and expected artifact, and an adapter binds it to a runner at execution time. Specs outlive runners.

intent.description: The step text from the scenario, verbatim. The agent is reproducing this behavior, not improvising around it.

techniques.description: The pinned identifiers from the scenario step. These are the lookup key an adapter uses to resolve a concrete emulation from a public library at run time.

actions.description: Abstract action set. States what must happen for the artifact to be produced, not the command that does it. The adapter resolves these against a published emulation library; the spec never carries payloads.

expected_artifacts.description: What this step should leave behind if the scenario's evidence row is right. Taken from the row's signal field, so the spec and the prediction cannot drift apart.

source.description: The exact system the artifact is claimed to land in, from the evidence row. The observer looks HERE first; finding it somewhere else is a different and reportable result.

detection_artifact.description: The named rule or saved search that is claimed to fire, from the row's evidence field. Absent when the row does not claim detection.

scoreable.description: Which claims this run may legitimately score, computed from the telemetry_pipeline mode. detection-fires is absent unless the pipeline is mirrored. An executor must not score a claim that is not listed here, and a scorecard that does is invalid.

requires_human.description: True when the step cannot be executed unattended at the current rung. The agent stops and asks.

out_of_scope.description: Parts of the scenario step this run deliberately does not reproduce, and why. A step that reaches a third party in the story becomes a local stand-in here, and saying so keeps the result readable.

excluded_steps.description: Steps the readiness validation ruled out, kept in the spec so the exclusion is visible on the scorecard rather than silently shrinking the denominator.

readiness.description: The result of the readiness validation that authorized this emission. Mechanical checks are recomputed by the emitter; the judgment fields come from the readiness prompt.
